A_level_at_the_page.question: Does a two-channel file leave the page (Stereo stage, default) at a different loudness over both channels than a one-channel file of the same file loudness, and by how much?
A_level_at_the_page.answer: Yes, systematically, by 3.01 dB. The stage law (engine.ts place()) puts a one-channel file on both sides at the balance 1/1 (azimuth 0), a two-channel file passes untouched, and BS.1770 counts a one-channel file as one channel. The page's own chain has a uniform -3 dB, so the energy over both channels at the page is the file's energy summed over its channels for one-channel files and 3.01 dB under it for two-channel files.
A_level_at_the_page.measure: AUDITION_URL=http://localhost:5231/dev/audition.html node tools/dev/audition-level.mjs <the 16 ids of the first run> --dry (own vite server, scratch ratings file); column file>page dB = 10*log10(energy over both channels at the page, 50 ms windows, whole play + 2 s / energy of the decoded file summed over its channels)

newSetOnScratchServer.note: file>page is a property of the page, so it stays; what changed is the energy of the two-channel files, which is now 3.01 dB higher

A_level_at_the_page.outlierNote: the two short one-channel thruster files read +0.29 and +0.33 dB; not explained (files of 0.4 to 0.8 s; I did not look into the window alignment of the recorder)
A_level_at_the_page.rule: listening copy loudness = BS.1770 integrated over the two channels the page plays; a one-channel file is counted on both, defined as its own loudness + 10*log10(2) (not by duplicating the file: for an event whose tail sits at the absolute gate the duplicated file read 1.82 dB higher instead of 3.01 dB, so the family target would no longer have put one-channel files where it put them; this was found by a test). Target = family target + 3.0103 dB for every candidate. No downmix.
A_level_at_the_page.afterAllProcessing: resampling, mean removal, ramp, end fade and the 10 ms of silence are done first for a gain, the level is measured on the result, the gain corrected and the copy made again, up to 30 times, bisecting when the loudness jumps; stops within 0.05 LU or at the true-peak ceiling (-1.1 dBFS), recorded as limitedByPeak with the level reached (lufsReachedPage, levelErrorDb)

B_cut_by_the_family_length.which_measurement_is_right: Both, for different questions. gear_2 s16 of MOSS (raw 4.0 s) is a steady sound at about -15 dB RMS for 3.6 s with a latch peak at 3.67 s (4 ms RMS maximum -6.2 dB). The cut ends at the cap 3.8 s inside the latch's decay. Last 50 ms before the cut against the loudest 4 ms (the script's own maximum, the rule): 11.0 dB under. Against the loudest 50 ms (-10.05 dB): 7.2 dB under, about what RESULTS.md says (6.6, same kind of measure on the 16-bit copy). Against the loudest 100 ms window (-11.34 dB) with a 100 ms window ending at 3.77 s, before the 30 ms fade: 0.1 to 0.5 dB under, which is what the audit calls 0.2 dB (100 ms window 3.06 dB under when ending at 3.8 s, 0.30 dB with 200 ms). So the longer the window, the nearer to the maximum a steady sound looks, and the more the transient maximum counts, the further it looks. The raw file itself is at -36 dB in its last 50 ms (4.0 s), which is why the end-of-file rule never fired.
B_cut_by_the_family_length.command: python script in the scratchpad on the scratch copy of moss/raw/gear_2__s16.wav, windows 4, 50, 100, 200 ms, hop 1 ms
B_cut_by_the_family_length.rule_now: an event that the cap cuts is cut off when the last 50 ms before the cut are within 20 dB of the same maximum (same window, same threshold as the end of the file); reason 'cut-off', cutOffAt 'family-length', lastDbBelowMaxAtCap recorded; an event that has died away 20 dB or more is kept and only marked capped

A first-sample or last-10-ms rule of -60 dBFS (the page's static check) let through a copy whose first sample was -60.4 dBFS: the recorder of the page flagged 4 clicks of 0.0005 to 0.001 in src_1_hull_4_sa3_p1s13 as page faults and the check failed. I lowered STEP_DB to -72 dBFS in screen.py (the recorder's dust floor is -70). More copies now get the 1.5 ms ramp and the 30 ms fade; the page's own rule (-60) in publish.py is unchanged.

BS.1770 integrated loudness of an event under about 0.5 s depends on how the 400 ms blocks fall: adding the 1.5 ms ramp to MOSS thruster_1 s12 (0.45 s) moved the gain for the same target from -8.7 to -6.2 dB (2.5 dB, peak -11.6 to -9.1 dBFS at the page). The loop measures the finished copy, so the target is met, but for such short events the LUFS target says little about how loud they are. The 'both dBFS' sounding level inside a family still differs by several dB between candidates (unweighted measure against K-weighting); not changed, as in RESULTS.md.
